Varronis Tarrutium " in primis Chaldaeicis rationibus eruditum , themate Romae
constiuto, illud fata urbis aeternae praenuntiasse post eventum invenit (Ciceron,
De Divin., II, p. 47, § 98; Bouché-Leclercq, Astrol. gr., p. 368 s.).
sections.en:
Varro's Tarrutius "learned especially in Chaldaean calculations", with the theme of Rome
established, found that it foretold the fates of the eternal city after the event (Cicero,
De Divin., II, p. 47, § 98; Bouché-Leclercq, Astrol. gr., p. 368 f.).

summary.headline: Defense of Astrological Learning
summary.text: Defense of astrological learning against charges of heresy, citing a mathematician’s prediction of Rome’s misfortunes, Saturn’s indication that citizens’ money would support monks, and the approval or practice of emperors, high priests, Gregory, and Basil.
